memory_leads.lead: A marine casualty should first be replayed as an occurrence and vessel/cargo/person safety state, not as a final cause or liability label. Collision, grounding, fire, flooding or machinery disablement can be observed before responsibility is known.

Distress notification and emergency communication create an early known-time layer involving the master/crew, owner/operator and relevant coastal or port authorities. Initial reports are operational signals and may be incomplete or revised.

Immediate casualty response prioritizes life safety and stabilization: damage control, fire response, flooding control, anchoring or other measures can change whether the vessel remains afloat, mobile, navigationally safe or able to continue toward a refuge/repair location.

Emergency towage and salvage are related but distinct assistance states. A disabled vessel may require towage or specialized salvage effort, while exact contractual characterization, rights and reward economics remain case-specific legal facts.

Salvage engagement introduces a multi-party state involving owner/operator, salvors, insurers/P&I and sometimes cargo interests or authorities. Appointment or intervention can precede agreement on reward, security, contribution or liability.

A place-of-refuge or emergency-port decision is a coordination state rather than an automatic right to berth. Vessel condition, cargo hazard, environmental risk, port capability, authority approval and onward repair options can interact before access is resolved.

Refloating, temporary repair, towing to repair, permanent repair and return-to-service are separate recovery milestones. Effective fleet supply can remain constrained long after the casualty event itself ends.

A vessel that cannot economically or safely return to service can enter a wreck/constructive-loss-type operational pathway in which removal, marking, cargo recovery, pollution control or disposal become distinct projects. Exact legal status and cost allocation require Evidence.

Casualty response can create environmental or access constraints beyond hull damage: spill containment, hazardous cargo concerns, channel obstruction or debris may affect ports and nearby traffic even when only one vessel is directly damaged.

General-average-style memory is structurally a deliberate sacrifice or extraordinary expenditure for common maritime safety followed by declaration/security/adjustment/contribution states. Whether a particular event qualifies or how contribution is calculated is a legal/adjustment question outside blind Memory.

Cargo interests may face recovery, forwarding, transshipment, storage, security or delayed-delivery states after a casualty. Physical cargo preservation and delivery can therefore diverge from the vessel's own recovery timeline.

Casualty investigation is a distinct information-production process. Evidence collection, interviews, technical examination and report publication can occur after operational recovery, and safety-oriented findings should not be silently collapsed into civil or criminal liability conclusions.

Casualty severity propagates through effective capacity, charter performance, cargo delivery, port access, insurance claims, financing and asset value on different clocks. One incident can therefore create several overlapping but non-identical operational and financial trajectories.
P053 survey memory is refined because condition/damage observations can support casualty stabilization and investigation, but observation, causal inference and final fault remain separate layers.

P044 insurance/P&I memory is refined because casualty response produces claim-notification, survey, security and loss-mitigation inputs before coverage, adjustment, recovery and liability are resolved.

P051 chartering memory is refined because a casualty can interrupt hire/freight performance, cargo delivery and vessel availability while the contractual off-hire, deviation, termination or damages consequences remain clause- and fact-specific.
P052 port-call memory is refined because emergency refuge, casualty access and wreck/channel constraints involve authority and service coordination outside an ordinary scheduled port call.

The atlas already recalls that chokepoints, accidents and operational disruptions can absorb effective capacity; P054 adds the casualty-response state machine rather than repeating disruption as a generic shock.
Earlier Shipping passes already separate physical readiness, legal availability, insurance and claims. P054 composes those layers around a casualty without creating new semantic owners.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: Specific casualty facts and causation/liability conclusions require official, technical, legal and claim-scoped Evidence.
Contract rights, salvage awards, guarantees, contribution bases and adjustment calculations are transaction-specific legal/financial facts.
Investigation purpose, authority, findings and downstream legal effect vary by jurisdiction and exact vintage.
Provider identity, current capability and event participation are source-first factual questions outside blind Memory.

stop_reason: The casualty-response lifecycle is populated from occurrence/distress and immediate stabilization through towage/salvage, refuge, refloat/repair or wreck removal, cargo recovery, sacrifice/security/contribution and casualty reporting/investigation, plus propagation into capacity, chartering and claims. Further recall becomes event-, contract-, award-, cause-, fault-, cost-, adjustment-, authority- or jurisdiction-specific.
truth_boundary: Memory-only orientation and not legal, safety, salvage, insurance or operational advice; no casualty chronology, cause, fault, liability, salvage/towage right, reward, security, general-average qualification or adjustment, investigation finding, wreck-removal obligation, port/refuge decision or provider capability is verified.
